section_summary: This section follows Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation’s effort to register a GTD mark in Japan. Its lawyers challenged the Japanese Patent Office’s reliance on a later registration held by Susumu Nakagawa, filed an appeal and an invalidation suit, and kept the State Department informed. The final pages begin a separate opposition to F. Matsumura’s proposed OTD mark.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Payne on GTD registration
subfiles.about: The Department discusses an appeal and possible diplomatic representations over the rejected GTD application.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton notes the February 5 appeal deadline and offers to have the ambassador discuss the case with Japanese authorities if Greenfield supplies details and legal arguments.

subfiles.title: Greenfield letter to its patent attorneys
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield reports seeking State Department help over its rejected GTD application.
subfiles.summary: Smith encloses Payne’s letter to Moore and promises to report the reply.

subfiles.title: Payne’s appeal to the State Department
subfiles.from: F. H. Payne, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Payne protests refusal of the GTD panel mark because of Nakagawa’s later registration.
subfiles.summary: Payne recounts Greenfield’s registrations from 1921 and 1925, quotes its lawyers’ account of the Japanese refusal, and asks for assistance before the February 1939 appeal deadline.

subfiles.title: Report of renewed Japanese refusal
subfiles.about: The Japanese office again rejects application 19741 because of registration 212580.
subfiles.summary: The firm translates the decision, says its priority argument failed, and advises that an appeal may cost $50–$75 without assurance of success.

subfiles.title: Report on argument filed against citation
subfiles.about: The firm reports filing an argument based on Greenfield’s older Japanese registrations.
subfiles.summary: Its Japanese associate doubts success because examiners disregard earlier office errors.

subfiles.title: Advice from Asamura and Higuchi relayed to Greenfield
subfiles.about: The attorneys relay Japanese advice about the obstacle posed by registration 212580.
subfiles.summary: They quote Asamura and Higuchi’s view that the cited mark remains effective until invalidated, despite Greenfield’s older marks.

subfiles.title: Instructions for rehearing
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan arranges a rehearing and explains the breadth of the cited Class 17 registration.
subfiles.summary: The associate will argue Greenfield’s earlier GTD registrations; the cited registration apparently covers all Class 17 goods.

subfiles.title: Authorization to contest the cited mark
subfiles.about: The attorneys authorize an effort to overcome registration 212580.
subfiles.summary: They question whether Nakagawa’s goods conflict with Greenfield’s and approve the proposed argument.

subfiles.title: Reminder of deadline to answer objection
subfiles.about: The firm requests instructions before the July 19 answer deadline.
subfiles.summary: It seeks directions for further prosecution of application 19741.

subfiles.title: Asamura and Higuchi’s opinion on the cited registration
subfiles.about: Japanese counsel assesses the chances of overcoming registration 212580.
subfiles.summary: They believe the office overlooked Greenfield’s older marks but will treat the cited registration as effective unless invalidated.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese counsel’s suggestions
subfiles.about: The attorneys seek advice on presenting the GTD application to the Japanese Patent Office.
subfiles.summary: They enclose earlier correspondence and question the breadth of Class 17 protection.

subfiles.title: Greenfield authorizes an argument and hearing
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield directs its attorneys to contest the citation against its GTD application.
subfiles.summary: Smith authorizes a written argument and personal hearing, and asks for Asamura and Higuchi’s advice.

subfiles.title: Initial report of objection to application 19741
subfiles.about: The attorneys explain the examiner’s citation of Nakagawa’s 1930 GTD registration.
subfiles.summary: They describe Greenfield’s earlier marks, propose an argument and hearing, estimate the expense, and note the July 19 deadline.

subfiles.title: Sketch of cited Japanese mark
subfiles.about: A sketch depicts the Japanese G.T.D. mark cited against Greenfield.
subfiles.summary: Sketch of registration 212580’s letter mark.

subfiles.title: Langner report of Japanese objection
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan reports the objection to application 19741 and proposes a response.
subfiles.summary: He contrasts Nakagawa’s 1930 registration with Greenfield’s earlier marks, proposes an argument and hearing, and gives a $35 estimate.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of filing report
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield acknowledges notice that its Class 17 application was filed.
subfiles.summary: Smith acknowledges application number 19741 and the listed goods.

subfiles.title: Notice of filing application 19741
subfiles.about: The attorneys report the filing date, number and goods for the GTD panel application.
subfiles.summary: Application 19741 was filed August 25, 1937, for Class 17 machinery and associated with two earlier registrations.

subfiles.title: Associate’s report of filing application 19741
subfiles.about: The firm confirms the Japanese filing and its association with Greenfield’s earlier marks.
subfiles.summary: It reports the August 25 filing, application number and Class 17 goods.

subfiles.title: Receipt of application documents
subfiles.about: The firm receives executed forms for GTD applications in three classes.
subfiles.summary: It will instruct the Japanese associate to file in Classes 8, 17 and 19.

subfiles.title: Executed powers and certificates returned
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield returns signed documents for Japanese trademark applications.
subfiles.summary: Smith sends powers of attorney and corporate nationality certificates.

subfiles.title: Request to sign application documents
subfiles.about: The attorneys send forms needed for applications in Japan.
subfiles.summary: They request signed powers of attorney and nationality certificates for Classes 8, 17 and 19.

subfiles.title: Authorization for additional GTD applications
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield approves filing the GTD rectangular panel mark in additional classes.
subfiles.summary: Smith accepts the associate’s proposal and authorizes the applications.

subfiles.title: Proposal to register the GTD panel mark in additional classes
subfiles.about: The attorneys propose further Japanese registrations for Greenfield’s GTD panel design.
subfiles.summary: After acceptance of a Class 19 application, they relay the associate’s recommendation to file the panel mark in Classes 8, 17 and 19.

subfiles.title: Print of proposed mark
subfiles.about: An enclosed print shows part of the proposed Greenfield trademark.
subfiles.summary: Surviving OCR captures only “CORPORATION” from the mark print.

subfiles.title: Payne forwards attorneys’ appeal report
subfiles.from: F. H. Payne, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Payne sends the Department an update on the Japanese GTD application.
subfiles.summary: He encloses the attorneys’ February 16 letter.

subfiles.title: Attorneys’ report quoting Japanese appeal advice
subfiles.about: The attorneys report that an appeal was filed and relay advice to invalidate Nakagawa’s mark.
subfiles.summary: They quote Asamura and Higuchi on Japanese trademark law and court decisions: Greenfield’s earlier associated marks may not overcome the cited mark, making invalidation proceedings advisable. They also note a pending appeal in another trademark dispute.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Edwards, Bower and Pool
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges correspondence about Greenfield’s GTD registration.
subfiles.summary: A copy and enclosures are forwarded to Ambassador Grew.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Payne
subfiles.about: Hamilton acknowledges Payne’s February 18 letter and enclosure.
subfiles.summary: He forwards them to Ambassador Grew for information.

subfiles.title: State Department instruction to Grew
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department sends recent GTD correspondence to its ambassador in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: It encloses letters from the attorneys and Payne with supporting papers.

subfiles.title: Attorneys’ cover letter updating State Department file
subfiles.about: The attorneys send correspondence on the GTD appeal and invalidation suit.
subfiles.summary: A list identifies enclosed letters dated February through November 1939.

subfiles.title: File update to Asamura and Higuchi
subfiles.about: The attorneys send correspondence to update Japanese counsel’s file.
subfiles.summary: Enclosures include State Department and Langner letters.

subfiles.title: Notice that the GTD appeal was filed
subfiles.about: The attorneys inform Greenfield that its Japanese appeal has been filed.
subfiles.summary: They enclose their letter to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Duplicate appeal report to Greenfield
subfiles.about: This copy reports the filed appeal and recommends invalidating registration 212580.
subfiles.summary: It repeats the February 16 report on Article 2 of Japanese trademark law, decisions concerning associated marks, and the pending dispute over registration 255570.

subfiles.title: Greenfield acknowledgment of appeal report
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield assumes its attorneys will take necessary action, including invalidation proceedings.
subfiles.summary: Smith says the February 16 letter will be forwarded to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Langner report on appeal and proposed invalidation
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan confirms the appeal and conveys Japanese counsel’s recommendation to attack Nakagawa’s registration.
subfiles.summary: The letter quotes counsel’s legal analysis, explains the basis for an invalidation suit, and asks for instructions. It also reports that an adverse party appealed a decision concerning registration 255570.

subfiles.title: Judges assigned to Greenfield’s appeal
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan reports the appeal number and assigned judges.
subfiles.summary: Appeal No. 90 of 1939 is assigned to Y. Minami, N. Kanishi and T. Ikedada.

subfiles.title: Japanese counsel acknowledges file update
subfiles.about: Japanese counsel acknowledges the February 14 correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Higuchi confirms the GTD matter has the firm’s attention.

subfiles.title: Request for invalidation cost estimate
subfiles.about: The attorneys ask the likely cost of invalidating Nakagawa’s registration.
subfiles.summary: They request an estimate for proceedings against registration 212580.

subfiles.title: Invalidation cost estimate
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan estimates the expense of an invalidation action.
subfiles.summary: The expected cost is $250–$300, barring unforeseen circumstances.

subfiles.title: Cost estimate relayed to Greenfield
subfiles.about: The attorneys advise Greenfield of the projected invalidation expense.
subfiles.summary: They expect a cost near $300 and propose proceeding unless Greenfield objects.

subfiles.title: Instruction to commence invalidation
subfiles.about: The attorneys authorize invalidation proceedings against Nakagawa’s trademark.
subfiles.summary: They accept the estimate and direct the firm to proceed.

subfiles.title: Request for evidence of GTD use in Japan
subfiles.about: The attorneys seek evidence for the invalidation suit.
subfiles.summary: They request an executed power of attorney and records of first and continuing Japanese use, including labels, catalogues, advertisements, representatives and customers.

subfiles.title: Greenfield supplies evidence for invalidation suit
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield returns the power of attorney and supplies material showing GTD use in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Smith encloses correspondence extracts, labels and customer names, identifies Muller, Phipps & Sellers as representative, and sends a catalogue separately.

subfiles.title: Extracts concerning earlier GTD use
subfiles.about: Extracts describe evidence that Greenfield’s GTD mark had been used in Japan since 1916.
subfiles.summary: They cite affidavits and correspondence about use and recognition of the mark.

subfiles.title: List of Greenfield customers in Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet lists Japanese customers relevant to proof of trade.
subfiles.summary: Customers and addresses in Tokyo and Osaka are listed.

subfiles.title: Evidence sent to Langner
subfiles.about: The attorneys forward Greenfield’s documents for the invalidation case.
subfiles.summary: They send the power of attorney, labels, correspondence extracts and customer list.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment and request for user affidavits
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan forwards the evidence to Japanese counsel and seeks proof of trademark use.
subfiles.summary: The associate will seek affidavits with help from Greenfield’s Osaka representative.

subfiles.title: Report that invalidation suit was filed
subfiles.about: The attorneys report filing suit to invalidate registration 212580.
subfiles.summary: They quote Japanese counsel’s account of the arguments and supporting advertisements and affidavits, and enclose the Japanese brief.

subfiles.title: Judges assigned to invalidation suit
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan reports the invalidation case number and assigned judges.
subfiles.summary: Suit No. 195 is assigned to T. Matsuoka, K. Numazawa and K. Sanuki.

subfiles.title: Japanese associate’s report on Nakagawa’s defense
subfiles.about: The associate reports Nakagawa’s counterstatement and its rebuttal in the invalidation suit.
subfiles.summary: Nakagawa argues that his GTD mark differs from Greenfield’s supposed “three mountains” mark and supplies affidavits. The associate replies that GTD dominates Greenfield’s marks and seeks confirmation from its Osaka representative.

subfiles.title: Attorneys’ update on invalidation litigation
subfiles.about: The attorneys explain Nakagawa’s counterstatement and their associate’s rebuttal.
subfiles.summary: They enclose the associate’s report and Japanese brief, and ask whether additional declarations should answer Nakagawa’s evidence.

subfiles.title: Greenfield asks about updating State Department
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Smith asks whether the State Department should receive the latest case correspondence.
subfiles.summary: He offers to send copies if the attorneys advise it.

subfiles.title: Attorneys’ cover letter on Matsumura opposition
subfiles.about: The attorneys send correspondence about Greenfield’s unsuccessful opposition to Matsumura’s OTD mark.
subfiles.summary: They say Japanese treatment of the mark’s pronunciation conflicts with its position in the Nakagawa case.

subfiles.title: Notice of Matsumura’s trademark application
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan alerts the attorneys to Matsumura’s proposed OTD mark.
subfiles.summary: He supplies application details and the November 1 opposition deadline.

subfiles.title: Matsumura application reported to Greenfield
subfiles.about: The attorneys forward notice of Matsumura’s Class 17 OTD application.
subfiles.summary: They give the application particulars and opposition deadline.

subfiles.title: Greenfield authorizes opposition to OTD
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield decides Matsumura’s mark is too similar to its own.
subfiles.summary: Smith directs the attorneys to oppose application 10260.

subfiles.title: Cable instructions to oppose Matsumura’s mark
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan confirms opposition instructions and requests a power of attorney.
subfiles.summary: The opposition will rely on Greenfield’s prior Class 17 registrations.

subfiles.title: Request for opposition power of attorney
subfiles.about: The attorneys request an executed power for the OTD opposition.
subfiles.summary: They ask Greenfield to sign and notarize the form.

subfiles.title: Executed power returned by Greenfield
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield returns the signed opposition power of attorney.
subfiles.summary: Smith confirms notarization.

subfiles.title: Power of attorney forwarded to Langner
subfiles.about: The attorneys forward Greenfield’s executed power for the Matsumura opposition.
subfiles.summary: The form supports opposition to application 10260.

subfiles.title: Report that OTD opposition was filed
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: Logan reports that the Japanese associate opposed Matsumura’s application.
subfiles.summary: The opposition cites Greenfield’s earlier registrations; a Japanese brief was filed.
